title: Plugin list deadline does not bound process exit: a grandchild holding the pipes keeps quest alive past it
description: From lore-cli via opum-agent OPAG-448 AC3 (2)(a). lore-cli found its port of our adapter carried this and fixed it in opum-ai/lore-cli#291, merged dev dc09ca98 (pre-squash fix 277aeb31), src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts bunPluginCommandRunner: spawn the runtime detached, on the deadline process.kill(-pid, SIGKILL) and cancel() both stdout/stderr readers; on win32 child.kill plus the cancel. Only the group kill reaps the grandchild; the cancel alone gets exit to about 1s and leaves it alive. MEASURED HERE 2026-09-26 at origin/dev f21783a: a fake codex running `trap "" TERM; sleep 12 & sleep 12`, CliAgentPluginPort listTimeoutMs 2000. The report settled at 2.002s ("did not finish within 2s") and the process exited at 12.067s, when the grandchild ended. src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts run() does child.kill(SIGKILL) plus unref(), which releases the child handle but not the pending Response(child.stdout).text() reads. The same run() serves the 600s update path.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On the deadline, run() kills the runtime process group (POSIX, spawned detached) and cancels both pipe readers; on win32 it kills the child and cancels the readers

A test using a fake runtime whose backgrounded grandchild holds the pipes times the REAL quest process exit and asserts it is bounded by the deadline plus a small margin, and that the grandchild is gone
The fix is cited against lore-cli dc09ca98 / 277aeb31, and bun run check exits 0

plan: 1. Spawn the runtime detached on POSIX; on the deadline or the output cap, process.kill(-pid, SIGKILL), falling back to child.kill on win32; keep the reader cancel QCLI-380 added
2. QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS_TIMEOUT_MS overrides the 15s list deadline, so a test can time the real CLI exit (mirrors lore LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS_TIMEOUT_MS)
3. Test the real quest process exit against a pipe-holding grandchild, in its own group and in the runtime group, with mutation controls
implementationNotes: IMPLEMENTED on fix/qcli-378-plugin-deadline-group-kill, stacked on QCLI-380 (b496831), because QCLI-380 rewrote run() over stream readers and already cancels them on stop. MEASURED STEPWISE with a fake codex (trap TERM; sleep 12 & ; sleep 12) and a 2s deadline. Before QCLI-380 (f21783a): settled 2.002s, exited 12.067s. With the QCLI-380 reader cancel only: exited 2.003s, grandchild ALIVE after quest exit, which reproduces lore-cli exactly. With the group kill added: exited 2.006s, grandchild gone. CHANGE src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts: detached spawn on POSIX, and stop() runs process.kill(-child.pid, SIGKILL), or child.kill on win32, inside try/catch. src/cli/composition.ts: QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS_TIMEOUT_MS overrides the list deadline; unset, non-numeric or non-positive keeps 15s. Like QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS it is an internal knob, undocumented in help. TESTS test/qcli378-plugin-deadline-bounds-exit.test.ts, which times the REAL quest CLI exit with a 500ms deadline and a 20s grandchild. Case A: the grandchild is in the runtime group; exit under 5s and the grandchild is dead. Case B: the grandchild is in its own group (set -m); exit under 5s and the grandchild alive, because the cancel alone bounds the exit. CONTROLS, predicted before running, all exact: M1 kills only the child, A red on alive (true); M2 removes the reader cancel, B red on elapsed (20170ms) and A green; M3 does neither, A red on elapsed (20154ms). The first run of M2 had only case A and stayed green, as predicted, which showed the cancel was unpinned and is why case B exists. bun run check exit 0, 678 pass. The win32 branch is not exercised: no win32 runner here.
